# Review of iliad-142 (Iliad 22.405–515)

Two passes over `units.json` (60 units). `gloss.json` did not exist at review time, so the second pass was a
second full units pass (labels and cross-references re-checked, Greek → `l` → `i` re-read). `t` is untouched
(checked: the concatenated `t` equals the packet's 111 lines; every `ln` agrees with the first line of its `t`;
every `l` has the line division of its `t`). Paragraph flags `p` fall at 405, 429, 437, 460, 515 as in the packet.
Quotation marks checked: Priam 416–428 (“ on unit 6, ” on unit 13), Hecuba 431–436 (units 16–18), Andromache's
first speech 450–459 (units 25–30), her long speech 477–514 (units 39–58, ” on unit 58), with the boy's words at
498 in single marks inside it (unit 51, `mark` present). Each speech's first unit has `mark`. iliad-141 ends at
22.404 with no speech running on, so there is no continuity to carry. Scansion flags: none, so no hand scansion
was required. Repeated lines (22.424, 22.436, 22.459, 22.515) agree with the shipped English.

No rendering in `new-renderings.md` changed, so that file was not edited. (The two `i` edits at 454 and 456 are

## Findings considered and refused

- 405–407 (unit 1) `l` "away from her flung": the added "from her" is English idiom for ἀπὸ … ἔρριψε; the object is not
  misrepresented. Kept.
- 473–474 (unit 37) `i` "close to death" for ἀτυζομένην ἀπολέσθαι: an interpretation, but the note explains it and
  `l` keeps the literal "to perish". Kept.
- 496 (unit 50) `i` "a boy whose parents are both living" for ἀμφιθαλής, and 510 (unit 57) `i` "your clothes" for the
  particle τοι: both are in the packet's table with the reason, and the notes say so. Kept.
- 479–481 (unit 40) `i` "I grimly fated" against `l` "me dread-fated": case shifts for English sense, approved in the
  packet. Kept.
- 451–452 (unit 26) πάλλεται rendered "leaps" and 460–461 παλλομένη "leaping": consistent with the table row. Kept.
- 502 (unit 53) λέκτροισιν `l` "in beds" / `i` "in a bed": plural of ordinary poetic usage; the two layers differ only in
  number. Kept.
- 431 (unit 16) βείομαι "epic form of the future of βιόω": accepted (it may also be read as a subjunctive; the sense is
  unaffected).
- 427 (unit 13) κορεσσάμεθα with κε read as past-potential "would have had our fill": the alternative (subjunctive) gives
  the same English with this context. Kept.
- No stock epithet is left untranslated; all house renderings checked against the
  table (ἐλεεινά, ὀβριμοεργός, ἀτάσθαλος, δαμάζω, λιπαρός, κορυθαίολος, ἀποτμήγω, ἐρύομαι, ἔρρω, τιθήνη, ἀτύζομαι, κόπρος,
  ἁδινός, ἐξάρχω, αἰνόμορος, ἄλγε’ ἔθηκε): all agree.
- Cross-references verified: 16.808, 12.454, 6.402–403 (Σκαμάνδριος, Ἀστυάναξ), 4.4, 1.2, 17.671/iliad-114, and the notes'
  internal references to 430, 445, 462, 480, 500 are true.

Nothing unresolved; no line is metrically flagged; nothing needs QUESTIONS.md.

## Gloss pass

`gloss.json` checked against `units.json` and the root `iliad-glossary.json`: 138 novel-form entries (all 138 forms of
`novel-forms.json` present, none already in the glossary, none extra) and 41 `__broaden__` entries. Every `__broaden__`
entry was confirmed to be the old glossary entry whole plus ` · ` plus a new reading, and each new reading was checked
against the line(s) where the form stands. Format: only typographic ’, all novel entries under 230 characters, no line
numbers, no "here".

### Changes (key · what was wrong · done)

| Key | What was wrong | What was done |
|---|---|---|
| κρήδεμνόν | Said the following enclitic was "θε"; there is no such enclitic. It is τε, elided before the rough breathing of ὅ (written θ’). | Now "enclitic τε that follows, elided θ’". |
| ἔρυσο | Named εἴρυσο as the Attic equivalent; εἴρυσο is itself Homeric. | Now "= Attic ἐρρύου, from ῥύομαι". |
| πληθυῖ | Homeric dative with no Attic equivalent named. | Added "(epic -υῖ = Attic πλήθει)". |
| ἀστυάναξ | "in apposition to πάϊς" is true of the first occurrence only; at 22.506 the name is the subject of πάθῃσι. | Now "in apposition to πάϊς, or itself the named subject". |
| ἥ (new `__broaden__`) | Existing entry covers ἥ before enclitic οἱ only; the part has relative ἥ before enclitic μιν (ἥ μιν ἔτικτε, ἥ μιν ἔχεσκ’). | Old entry whole + new reading. |
| ἐκάλυψεν (new `__broaden__`) | Existing entry reads "with περί in tmesis, ’wrapped round’"; here it is κατ’ ὀφθαλμῶν … ἐκάλυψεν, night covering the eyes, no περί. | Old entry whole + new reading. |
| ἑοῦ (new `__broaden__`) | Existing entry says "agreeing with παιδός"; here ἑοῦ agrees with πατρός (ἑοῦ ἐπὶ γούνασι πατρός). | Old entry whole + new reading (old entry itself left alone). |

Total: 4 novel entries corrected, 3 `__broaden__` entries added (41 → 44 broadened keys in all).

### Considered and refused

- αἰδέσσεται as future vs. short-vowel aorist subjunctive after ἤν πως: either is possible; the future parse is defensible and the translation is the same. Left.
- θαλέων (θάλεα), δαιτύος (fem.), εἰνατέρες: parses are right; no Attic equivalent exists or is attested to name. Left.
- ὅ as conjunction "that" after a verb of perceiving (οὐδ’ ἐνόησεν ὅ …): true of the line; the old entry's "seeing" reading is close but the new reading is separately stated and correct. Left.
- ἥ (relative, fem. nom.) at 22.457 referring to ἀγηνορίης: covered by the same new reading ("who, which").
- The 41 original `__broaden__` entries: each new reading is true of its line; no example translation contradicts the Greek. Left unchanged.
- Known forms with a single-reading glossary entry (e.g. ἐπὶ, κατὰ, μετὰ, τῆς, τῷ): scanned against the lines; their existing readings cover the uses in this part. Left.
